question: A 55-year-old man with HIV on antiretroviral therapy comes to the physician for a follow-up examination. His HIV viral load is 559 copies/mL (N<49). His physician is concerned about the development of drug resistance. The result of HIV genotype testing shows reduced viral susceptibility to darunavir and ritonavir. Which of the following molecular processes is most likely affected by this mutation?

options.opa: Integration of DNA into the host genome
options.opb: Synthesis of DNA from an RNA template
options.ope: Binding of glycoproteins to T-cell receptors

paths: (darunavir)-TREATS->(Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome)-INTERACTS_WITH->(Human T-lymphotropic virus 1)-LOCATION_OF->(RNA-Directed DNA Polymerase)
(darunavir)-TREATS->(Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome)-INTERACTS_WITH->(Human T-lymphotropic virus 1)-LOCATION_OF->(RNA-Directed DNA Polymerase)

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Reduced viral susceptibility to darunavir and ritonavir -> Mutation in protease gene -> Impaired cleavage of viral polyproteins -> Reduced production of functional viral proteins -> Modification of translated proteins -> 80%
CHAIN: Reduced viral susceptibility to darunavir and ritonavir -> Mutation in reverse transcriptase gene -> Altered enzyme activity -> Impaired synthesis of DNA from an RNA template -> 75%
enhanced_information: Mutation in the protease gene leading to reduced viral susceptibility to darunavir and ritonavir affects the modification of translated proteins. This mutation impairs the cleavage of viral polyproteins, resulting in reduced production of functional viral proteins, ultimately impacting the modification of translated proteins.
analysis: The mutation in the protease gene leading to reduced viral susceptibility to darunavir and ritonavir affects the cleavage of viral polyproteins, impacting the modification of translated proteins. This aligns with the known function of protease in viral replication. The mutation impairs the processing of viral proteins, ultimately affecting the modification of translated proteins.
